source.title: Modeling Transformers as complex networks to analyze learning dynamics

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses induction heads as motivation, but its own measurements concern component-level graph structure and a single induction-task prediction. It does not measure induction heads, their mechanism, or the in-context-learning and loss-curve measures named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the induction-head phase-change account as background. Its own results measure causal-influence graphs and correct-token logit on one fixed task; these are recorded as related findings, not as tests of the listed versions. No results cited from other work are recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses a single repeated-name induction prompt as a testbed for its own method, component-level causal-influence graphs built by zero-ablation. It reports only graph metrics and one correct-token logit across Pythia-14M checkpoints. It never identifies induction or previous-token heads, never measures loss by token index or a training-loss bump, and never varies data, models or architectures. So no result bears on V1–V7 as stated. The multi-phase graph evolution is about graph structure, not induction-head formation, so it does not test V7. The single-prompt logit rise is not the ICL measure of V2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but one part is the reader's framing. The authors state the results support their hypothesis that a component-graph view reveals structural signatures of learning, including the phase change associated with induction-head formation. The graph shows multi-phase evolution: exploration, consolidation and pruning, then refinement, with stable spreader hubs. The authors do not themselves disclaim testing induction-head formation; that caveat comes from the reader, though it is accurate.
record.recipe_differences: Uses zero-ablation-based causal influence to construct component graphs and tracks graph metrics across Pythia-14M checkpoints. It does not use the original induction-head identification or ICL/loss-curve measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The graph is constructed at thresholds τ∈{0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 1.0}; the paper describes lower thresholds as producing sparser graphs and uses τ=0.7 for component heatmaps. It uses one fixed input sentence.

fits_no_version.finding: On one fixed repeated-name prompt, the correct-token logit rises steeply in roughly the first 20k steps. It then improves gradually again after graph pruning around 60k–80k steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In Pythia-14M, performance on a single induction-style prompt improves in more than one training phase.

fits_no_version.finding: Component-level causal-influence graphs evolve in several phases. Node and edge counts first grow, then are pruned. Edge weights become long-tailed. The spreader hubs (emb, mlp_0) stay stable, while gatherer and gatekeeper components reconfigure around 10k, 80k and 100k steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For one model and input, component-graph structure evolves through exploration, consolidation and refinement phases across training.

record.problems: The study uses a single small model and a single input sentence. The authors note that the graph may depend on the input and that zero-ablation is only one possible intervention. The graph metrics do not directly identify induction heads or measure the claim's ICL and loss-curve outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: None of the related graph-metric findings described in the results section were omitted.

untested.parts: No identification of induction or previous-token heads, and no test of composition or the [A][B]…[A]→[B] mechanism.
No induction-head emergence timing, no ICL score by token index, and no training-loss bump measured.
No large models; no attribution of ICL to induction heads.
Single model (pythia-14m); no cross-family, cross-size, cross-run or cross-modality comparison.
Training data and setup are not varied.
Phases are reported in graph metrics only; induction-head sub-steps are not measured.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'discusses/T6' is also defensible. T4 was chosen because the paper uses the induction task as a testbed for its own method. The paper is a single-author proof of concept. It uses one input, zero-ablation only, no controls and no uncertainty. pythia-14m is described as having 1.2M parameters, which is as stated in the paper but likely a misstatement. No verdicts are given because no row bears on any version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not identify induction heads, test composition with a previous-token head, or measure the general [A][B] … [A] → [B] mechanism.
Does not measure induction-head emergence, loss by token index, or a training-loss bump. The correct-token logit on one fixed task is not the claimed ICL measure.
Does not measure how much ICL in large transformers is carried by induction heads.
Uses one model and does not test induction behaviour across model families, sizes, runs, architectures, or modalities.
Does not vary the training data or setup, or measure persistence of ICL.
Does not test few-shot task learning or compare induction heads with other mechanisms.
Reports multiple phases in graph metrics, but does not measure induction-head formation or its sub-steps.

rows.value: The logit rises steeply during the initial graph-growth period; after a structural refinement around 60k–80k steps, it has a further period of gradual improvement.
rows.note: This is a performance proxy on one fixed prompt, not loss by token index or a measure of ICL generally.

conditions.value: Across training, with reconfigurations reported around ~10k and ~80k steps
Multiple thresholds for distributions; τ=0.7 for component heatmaps

rows.value: The distribution develops a right-skewed tail. High-in-degree components reconfigure over training; examples named include attn.z.2.3, heads in the 4th and 5th layers, mlp_2, mlp_5, and later a new set including heads in layer 3.
rows.note: These are graph authorities, not identified induction heads.
rows.check: The text says the first consolidation runs 'up to ~1 steps', likely a typo for ~10k. The row's '~10k' is an inference. High-in-degree components are graph authorities, not identified induction heads.

Multiple thresholds for distributions; τ=0.7 for component heatmaps

rows.value: Most components maintain low out-degree; emb and mlp_0 are described as a consistent hub set after ~10k steps, with attn.v.0 and attn.z.0 also named in the account of the shift from initial information sharing. Weaker spreaders appear from ~80k.
rows.note: These are graph spreaders, not induction heads.

rows.subject: pythia-14m

rows.operation_detail: Tracked betweenness centrality and components above the 95th percentile.

conditions.value: Across training; pathway changes described before and after 100k steps

rows.value: Most components have centrality zero. A core including mlp_1, mlp_2, mlp_3 and attn.z.2 emerges early; components including mlp_4 and attn.z.3/attn.z.4 are frequently central before 100k, then are largely superseded by other components.
rows.note: This measures graph gatekeepers, not induction-head sub-steps.
